title: Deriving the Cosine Difference Formula from the Sum Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the cosine addition formula \cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B together with even/odd identities to derive the difference formula \cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B.

steps.title: Express A - B as A + (-B) in the Cosine Sum Formula
steps.explanation: Replace B with -B in the standard cosine addition identity cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B.
steps.why: The addition formula holds universally for any real angle, including -B.

steps.title: Apply the Even/Odd Symmetry Identities
steps.explanation: Use the fact that cosine is an even function and sine is an odd function to simplify cos(-B) and sin(-B).
steps.why: Reflecting an angle B across the x-axis to -B preserves the x-coordinate (cosine) and negates the y-coordinate (sine).

steps.title: Substitute and Simplify Signs
steps.mathExpression: \cos(A - B) = \cos A (\cos B) - \sin A (-\sin B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B
steps.explanation: Substitute the simplified terms; the two negative signs in the second product cancel to produce a plus sign.
steps.why: Subtracting a negative product -sin A (-sin B) adds +sin A sin B.
